text:
noah: seeing a spike in Pod connection failures in eu-west3 GPU pool. Jobs are OOM/restarting because gRPC streams drop mid-request. Alert shows conntrack close to max on a handful of nodes (gpu-node-12, gpu-node-15).

miriam: I pulled /proc on gpu-node-12, looks like nf_conntrack_count is 262130 and nf_conntrack_max is 262144 — basically saturated. Heap of entries in TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED.

devon: copy of kernel conntrack summary:
```
# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
262130
# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
262144
# conntrack -L | tail -n 8
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.128.3.12 dst=10.128.7.4 sport=50122 dport=51010 packets=432 bytes=32211 src=10.128.7.4 dst=10.128.3.12 sport=51010 dport=50122 packets=128 bytes=9122 use=1
...
```
Entries are mostly pod->pod TCP to model-shard services on port 51010 and a ton of pod->s3 egress.

sara: this matches the timeline of the prefetch rollout yesterday — model-cache agent opened 40 concurrent fetch sockets per pod and doesn't reuse keepalive properly. A few noisy pods + autoscaler burst = conntrack flood.

noah: is RDMA involved? I saw some RDMA-enabled nodes in the pool. RDMA should be bypassing the kernel TCP stack, right?

miriam: RDMA traffic (ibverbs) bypasses TCP but our inference RPCs are still over TCP for the shard fetcher. RDMA-only workloads are fine. The problematic path is TCP NAT/SNAT on egress and inter-pod DNAT when routing across nodes.

devon: temporary mitigation we can apply immediately: bump nf_conntrack_max and reduce established timeout to recycle stale entries faster. Example commands to run as root (we can push via daemonset):
```sh
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600
# optionally flush really old TIME_WAIT entries (use with caution)
conntrack -L | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
```
This buys time but it's not a long-term fix.

alex: agree. Also add an iptables raw table rule to avoid tracking known internal short-lived flows:
```sh
# avoid conntrack for pod->s3 egress from our model-prefetch subnet
iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -s 10.128.0.0/14 -d 52.92.0.0/14 -p tcp -j NOTRACK
```
We need to be careful with NOTRACK and make the CIDRs precise.

sara: can we change the prefetch agent to reuse keepalive connections? That's the proper fix — reduce socket churn. Filing a ticket for the model-cache team now. In the interim: rate-limit prefetch concurrency per pod to 6.

noah: ops-bot telemetry shows kube-proxy on several nodes also hit high conntrack/iptables churn. Should we restart kube-proxy or switch modes (iptables -> ipvs)?

miriam: restarting kube-proxy might temporarily free up nf_conntrack entries created by kube-proxy NAT rules, but it's noisy. Switching to ipvs is a medium-term plan (requires drift testing). Short-term: roll a daemonset that applies sysctl bump and deploy an iptables NOTRACK for egress to S3 and internal cache ports. Then cordon + drain the most affected nodes to respawn pods and reduce simultaneous prefetchers.

devon: I'll prepare the daemonset YAML. It will run privileged and set sysctls and apply the iptables raw rule on startup. Also will instrument node-level metrics for conntrack_count.

alex: add a quick kube-apiserver admission check to block pods requesting >40 prefetch threads until the model-cache agent is patched. We should also add a rollout flag to the model-cache helm chart to ramp prefetch concurrency.

noah: sounds good. Action items:
- devon: deploy sysctl+raw-iptables daemonset to eu-west3 ASAP (5–10m)
- sara: open urgent bug for model-cache agent to reuse keepalive + add concurrency cap (P0)
- miriam: draft iptables CIDRs and validate NOTRACK safety with security (no bypass for egress policy enforcement)
- alex: schedule ipvs migration spike next week (low-risk cluster)

sara: started bug: INFRA-1892 'model-cache: socket reuse + concurrency cap' and added reproducer logs.

ops-bot: Scheduled daemonset rollout to eu-west3 (canary 2 nodes) — will wait for manual go from devon.

devon: canary applied to gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-15. conntrack_count dropped from 262130 -> 190420 in 90s after iptables raw rule and sysctl bump. Pods in canary nodes recovered.

noah: great. keep monitoring. After stable for an hour we can roll out region-wide and follow up with infra postmortem + model-cache patch. :thumbsup:

miriam: putting follow-up postmortem + config changes on the weekly eng-runtime retro.

alex: adding look into ephemeral port range on nodes and whether node-local NAT (e.g., Egress IP) could help reduce state by offloading to external load balancer.

noah: thanks everyone — I'm leaving oncall notes and will update the incident ticket with current mitigations.
